ai.description: The Ponmudi Day Gecko reaches 45 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow-spotted vertebral stripe and lacks enlarged tubercles on the flanks. It possesses a slender, flattened body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis nairi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its throat, which is absent in most other sympatric day geckos.
ai.habitat: The Ponmudi Day Gecko inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the southern Western Ghats, typically found on rock surfaces at altitudes between 900 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: The Ponmudi Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis nairi* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ponmudi Day Gecko is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations ranging from 800 to 1,100 meters.
